body:
After looking into this more, I think this is probably not a Forward+ bug.

The behavior seems to come from the interaction between discard inside light(), the depth/material prepass, and the background rendering order.

In Forward+, discard inside light() only runs during the lighting/color pass. It can prevent the material color from being written, but it does not participate in the earlier depth/material prepass, because light() is not evaluated there. As a result, the object can still write its full depth first.

Then, when the color pass reaches light() and discards the fragment, no material color is written. However, since the depth buffer already contains the object depth, the background/sky pass later does not fill those pixels as background. This leaves the existing clear/intermediate color visible, which appears as a dark mesh-shaped region.

This also explains why discard in fragment() behaves correctly: it runs early enough to affect the prepass, so the discarded pixels do not write object depth in the first place.

So I think the current behavior is technically consistent with how Forward+ is structured. The confusing part is that discard inside light() can look like a fragment visibility operation, while in practice it is too late to be used that way reliably.

Maybe the documentation could mention that discard in light() should not be used for object visibility/clipping, and that visibility-related discard should be done in fragment() instead.
